dva-med-085.text: A developer has used the application with the AWS X-Ray and he wants FILTRAR traces by business values (e.g. find all traces of customer 'client-123' or from applications above R$ 500). Which feature of X-Ray makes these values searchable in filter expressions?
options: Metadata, which is the indexed field for searches
Annotations: indexed key-value pairs, searchable in filter expressions (differently metadata, which is not indexed))
Put values in the segment name
Increase the sampling rate to 100%
dva-med-085.explanation: Annotations are indexed for trace search and clustering; metadata stores additional data rich but not searchable — recording business IDs as annotation is the practice for targeted investigations.
dva-med-085.hint: In X-Ray, one key-value pair enters the search index; the other is only 'annex' — which is which?
optionRationales: Annotations are indexed for trace search and clustering; metadata stores additional data rich but not searchable — recording business IDs as annotation is the practice for targeted investigations.
It's the reverse: metadata is NOT indexed — it serves an additional context; those who feed the searches are annotations.
Showing everything multiplies cost and volume, but does not make business values searchable — this requires annotations.
Segment names identify the service — pollute them with dynamic data breaks the service map and does not create search index.

dva-med-086.text: The cost of X-Ray has increased with the volume of traffic, and the team wants to continue tracking 100% of the requests of a critical endpoint of payments, but sample only a small fraction of the other routes. Which feature of X-Ray implements this control.?
options: Turn off X-Ray at peak times
Filter tracks after collected and pay for all
Save tracks manually to log files
Sampling custom rules, defining reservoirs/rates by service, route and method
dva-med-086.explanation: The sampling rules allow granularity by attributes of the request: 100% in the critical endpoint and reduced percentage in the remainder — balancing visibility and cost, with central update without redeployment.
dva-med-086.hint: The 'sampling rules' choose who enters the research: the VIP always, the crowd by sample.
optionRationales: The sampling rules allow granularity by attributes of the request: 100% in the critical endpoint and reduced percentage in the remainder — balancing visibility and cost, with central update without redeployment.
Blinding observability exactly when problems happen reverses the purpose of tracing.
The cost arises in the collection — filter then does not save; the sampling decides ANTES.
Home logs lose service map, correlation and X-Ray tools — do not replace sampling.

dva-med-087.text: An application records structured logs in CloudWatch Logs and the team wants one ALARME when the word 'ERROR' appear more than 50 times in 5 minutes in a log group. Which mechanism converts log occurrences into an alarmable metric?
options: Alarm directly on the log text, without metric
Increase log group retention
Metric filter in the log group, extracting the default occurrences for a custom metric used by the alarm
Export the logs to S3 and count on Athena from time to time
dva-med-087.explanation: The metric filter scans log events in real time and publishes the count (or value extracted) as a metric of the CloudWatch — on which the alarm with threshold and period is configured.
dva-med-087.hint: Text does not trigger alarm — first the 'filter' transforms the pattern into an accounting metric.
optionRationales: The metric filter scans log events in real time and publishes the count (or value extracted) as a metric of the CloudWatch — on which the alarm with threshold and period is configured.
Alarms of the CloudWatch operate on METRICS — the filter is the bridge that transforms text into number.
Batch analysis serves investigations — for minute alerts, real-time filter is the way.
Retention controls how long logs are stored — no metrics or alerts.

dva-med-088.text: One API REST no API Gateway returns intermittent errors and team needs visibility: (1) details of how the gateway processes each request (parameters, transformations, reason for errors) to debug; and (2) a standardized record of each call (IP, latency, status) for analysis. API Gateways match every need?
options: Execution logs for internal processing clearance and access logs for standardized registration by request
Access logs to debug transformations and execution logs for summary record
The API Gateway does not generate logs; only the backend loga
VPC Flow Logs cover both needs
dva-med-088.explanation: Execution logs detail the gateway's internal pipeline (useful and verbose, for temporary debug); access logs record a configurable line per call, ideal for continuous analysis and metrics of use.
dva-med-088.hint: One log is the 'X-ray of processing' (verbose, to debug); the other is the 'visit book' (one line per call)).
optionRationales: Execution logs detail the gateway's internal pipeline (useful and verbose, for temporary debug); access logs record a configurable line per call, ideal for continuous analysis and metrics of use.
It is inverted: the internal processing detail appears in the execution logs; the summary by request is the access log.
The gateway has both types of own logs, capable per stage — independent of the backend.
Flow Logs record flows of REDE the VPC — not processing HTTP of the API Gateway.

dva-med-089.text: Users report sporadic errors in a API serverless and metric 'Throttles' function Lambda shows values above zero in peaks. What this metric indicates and what is the first line of investigation?
options: Syntax errors in function code
Invocations rejected due to lack of available competition; investigate the account/function competition consumption and assess reserved competition or quota increase
Expiration of function logs
Slowness in the network of the Region
dva-med-089.explanation: Throttles count rejections by limit of competing executions: the diagnosis passes through ConcurrentExecutions versus quotas, and the correction combines reserves for critical functions, increase of limit or smoothing of traffic.
dva-med-089.hint: The metric counts the closed doors on the face of the invocations — the doorman is the limit of competition.
optionRationales: Throttles count rejections by limit of competing executions: the diagnosis passes through ConcurrentExecutions versus quotas, and the correction combines reserves for critical functions, increase of limit or smoothing of traffic.
Code gaps appear in Errors and logs — Throttles is Rejection ANTES to execute.
Network problems raise latency (Duration) — do not count as throttling.
Log retention does not interact with execution — Throttle Meter Meter Competition Limit.

dva-med-090.text: A table of the DynamoDB in provisioned mode shows peaks in ThrottledRequests metric, but the aggregate ConsumedCapacity is well below the provisioned. What hypothesis should the developer investigate first?
options: The table is corrupted and needs to be restored
Access concentration in few keys (hot partition): the limit is per partition, so a hot key suffers thrttle even with added capacity remaining
The IAM is blocking requests
Indexes GSI expired.
dva-med-090.explanation: Throttling with total free capacity is the classic signature of the hot partition — the investigation goes through CloudWatch Insights contributor and partition key redesign.
dva-med-090.hint: Capacity left + thrttle going on = someone is always hitting in the same drawer'.
optionRationales: Throttling with total free capacity is the classic signature of the hot partition — the investigation goes through CloudWatch Insights contributor and partition key redesign.
Throttling is traffic control, not corruption — restoration does not change access distribution.
Permission lock generates AccessDenied — does not count on Throttling metric.
GSIs do not expire — and the symptom described points to key distribution, not indexes.

dva-med-091.text: A team added the DAX in front of the DynamoDB to speed up readings, but realized that part of the calls continues to go straight to the bank without cash gain. Analysis showed that these calls use ConsistentRead=true. What is the explanation?
options: The DAX only cache tables with less than 1 GB
The DAX needs to be restarted daily to cache everything
The DAX attends the cache only possibly consistent readings; strongly consistent readings are passed directly to DynamoDB
The cluster DAX is on another account
dva-med-091.explanation: By design, or DAX does not serve strongly consistent cache read(s) — applications that require strong consistency do not benefit from DAX in these calls.
dva-med-091.hint: The accelerator serves the 'freeze' reading of the cache; whoever requires the certified data at the time drills the cache row.
optionRationales: By design, or DAX does not serve strongly consistent cache read(s) — applications that require strong consistency do not benefit from DAX in these calls.
There is no daily restart — the observed behavior is the documented semantic consistency.
Account configuration would generate connection/permission errors — no selective bypass by type of reading.
There is no such limit — the bypass criterion is the mode of consistency of reading.

dva-med-092.text: Consumers in a row SQS they are not following the production of messages, and the processing delay grows. SQS is the best indicator of this backlog and how it can guide automatic correction?
options: The average body size of the messages
NumberOfMessagesDeleted, showing future delay
The color of the row icon on the console
ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible: row size can feed an alarm/target tracking that scales consumers (ex: ASG or competition) as backlog grows
dva-med-092.explanation: The depth of the row is the production×consumption imbalance thermometer — using it (or the backlog by instance) as a consumer scaling metric closes the automatic correction cycle.
dva-med-092.hint: Tell me how many messages are 'in the waiting room' — and use that number to hire more attendants alone.
optionRationales: The depth of the row is the production×consumption imbalance thermometer — using it (or the backlog by instance) as a consumer scaling metric closes the automatic correction cycle.
Exclusions measure what has already been processed — accumulated backlog appears in visible messages waiting.
The non-color backlog console — serious monitoring uses metrics and alarms.
Average Payload reports unit weight — not accumulation of unprocessed messages.

dva-med-093.text: A function Lambda consumes a stream of Kinesis and the dashboard shows the IteratorAge metric growing continuously. What this means and what are the typical correction levers?
options: The stream's been empty for a long time.
The function is with excessive permissions
Processing is delayed in relation to the arrival of records (risk of expiring retention data); correct by accelerating the function, increasing parallelism factor/shards or batch size
Records are coming from the future with wrong timestamps
dva-med-093.explanation: IteratorAge measures the age of the last processed record: constant growth indicates slower consumption than production — corrections attack consumer throughput before records expire from the retention window.
dva-med-093.hint: It is the 'reader's delay' in relation to the treadmill: if it only grows, the reading needs more speed or more readers.
optionRationales: IteratorAge measures the age of the last processed record: constant growth indicates slower consumption than production — corrections attack consumer throughput before records expire from the retention window.
The metric measures the delay of CONSUMO — not the quality of producers' timestamps.
Ozy stream zero or delay — IteratorAge High requires traffic ENTRANDO Faster than it comes out..
Broad permissions are a matter of safety — they do not affect the stream's consumption speed.

dva-med-094.text: A route from API Gateway calls for processing that takes ~50 seconds, and TODAS calls return error 504 What limit explains the error and what architectural pattern the contour?
options: Error CORS in long calls
Lack of memory in API Gateway, which should be resized
The certificate TLS expired

The integration timeout of the API Gateway (~29 seconds in the pattern) is exceeded; the correction is the asynchronous pattern: the API thread/start work and return 202 with an ID for the customer consult the status
dva-med-094.explanation: The gateway does not indefinitely wait for the backend: long works must be uncoupled (SQS/Step Functions) with immediate response and polling/webhook completion — eliminating the 504 structural.
dva-med-094.hint: The gateway shuts down the call near the 29s — delayed work receives a 'service protocol' and rotates behind the scenes.
optionRationales: The gateway does not indefinitely wait for the backend: long works must be uncoupled (SQS/Step Functions) with immediate response and polling/webhook completion — eliminating the 504 structural.
The gateway is managed without memory dimensioning by the customer — the error arises from time, not from resources.
CORS lock in the browser with own errors — or 504 indicates timeout upstream.
Passed certificate fails the handshake immediately — not after 29 seconds of waiting.

dva-med-095.text: The latency alarm of a API uses the Media response time and never shoots, but users complain of severe sporadic slowness. What change in monitoring captures this real experience best?
options: Remove the alarm, since the average is healthy
Alarm about high percentages (p95/p99) of latency, which expose the slow tail diluted by the mean
Increase the alarm period to 24 hours
Change the mean to the minimum latency
dva-med-095.explanation: The average hides extremes: with 1% of the calls carrying 10s, p99 screams while the average sleeps — high percentages reflect the experience of the most affected users and are the standard for SLOs.
dva-med-095.hint: The average hides the 1% Unlucky; the 'p-ninety-and-so' put them in the spotlight.
optionRationales: The average hides extremes: with 1% of the calls carrying 10s, p99 screams while the average sleeps — high percentages reflect the experience of the most affected users and are the standard for SLOs.
The minimum shows the MELHOR called — even blinder to slow tail than average.
Long periods dilute peaks even more — the problem is statistics, not the window.
The users' complaint is the real signal — the monitoring is that you need to see it.

dva-med-096.text: In peak traffic, functions Lambda which access a RDS PostgreSQL start failing with 'FATAL: too many connections'. Each concurrent execution opens its own connection. Which service structurally resolves this exhaustion?
options: Create a read replica to receive excess writings
Reduce the timeout of functions to release connections
Amazon RDS Proxy between functions and the bank, multiplexing thousands of executions in a controlled connection pool
Increase max_connections indefinitely not parameter group
dva-med-096.explanation: The RDS Proxy shares and reuses connections, absorbing the explosive nature of the serverless without bursting the max_connections — in addition to speeding failovers and integrating with Secrets Manager.
dva-med-096.hint: Between the functions swarm and the bank, there is a lack of the 'connection porter' that recycles instead of opening new ones.
optionRationales: The RDS Proxy shares and reuses connections, absorbing the explosive nature of the serverless without bursting the max_connections — in addition to speeding failovers and integrating with Secrets Manager.
Each connection consumes the bank's memory — raising the roof without control only moves the collapse point.
Replicas do not accept written — do not absorb the transactional volume of functions.
Timeout minor kills legitimate executions — the problem is the absence of pooling, not the duration.
